title: Finding Common Ground: HCF and LCM
seo_title: Finding Common Ground Class 7 Worksheet with Answers (Ganita Prakash Part 2, Chapter 3)
standard_code: Class 7, Ganita Prakash Part 2, Chapter 3: Finding Common Ground
standard_text: Common factors and common multiples, highest common factor (HCF) and lowest common multiple (LCM) by listing and by prime factorisation, and their use in problems (summary of NCERT Ganita Prakash Class 7)
meta_desc: Class 7 Finding Common Ground worksheet (Ganita Prakash Part 2, Chapter 3): HCF, LCM, prime factorisation, HCF × LCM and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: HCF × LCM = the product of the two numbers
key_sub: HCF: the largest number dividing both. LCM: the smallest number both divide.
body_html:
How it works

The HCF (highest common factor) is the largest number that divides all the given numbers. The LCM (lowest common multiple) is the smallest number that is a multiple of all of them.

With prime factors: 24 = 2³ × 3 and 36 = 2² × 3². HCF takes the lower powers: 2² × 3 = 12. LCM takes the higher powers: 2³ × 3² = 72.

For two numbers, HCF × LCM = product: 12 × 72 = 24 × 36.

Example

Find the HCF and LCM of 18 and 24.

18 = 2 × 3²

24 = 2³ × 3

Answer: HCF 6, LCM 72

Example

Two bells ring every 6 and 8 minutes. When do they ring together again?

LCM of 6 and 8

Answer: After 24 minutes

Common mistakes

  • Taking the product of the two numbers as the LCM.
  • Taking the smaller number as the HCF.
  • Using HCF where the problem needs LCM (things happening together again).

faq.q: What is the difference between HCF and LCM?
faq.a: The HCF is the largest common factor; the LCM is the smallest common multiple.

faq.q: When do we use the LCM in a problem?
faq.a: When things repeat and we want them to happen together again, such as bells or buses.

faq.q: When do we use the HCF in a problem?
faq.a: When we cut or share into the largest equal groups or pieces.

items.q: Find the highest common factor (HCF) of 24 and 36.
items.e: Factors of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. Factors of 36: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. The biggest number in both lists is 12.

items.q: Write 112 as a product of prime factors in index form.
